meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: 話してきます combines 話して ('talk and') with きます ('come back') to mean 'I will go talk to them and return'.

examples.text: 少し社長と話してきます。
examples.trans: I will go talk with the president for a bit.

examples.text: ゆっくり話しましょう。

meanings.note: Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Humble/plain term for one's own father.

examples.trans: My father is an office worker.
Words I learned from my father.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Expresses frustration, regret, or surprise that reality contradicts what was expected; often trails off at the end of a spoken complaint.

examples.text: 約束したのに来なかった。
examples.trans: Even though they promised, they did not come.

examples.text: せっかくの休みなのに。
examples.trans: Even though it is a hard-earned day off.

meanings.note: Na-adjective.

examples.text: とても立派な建物ですね。
立派な大人になりましたね。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: 何で父親がいないのに、こんな立派な暮らしができるのかなって。
examples.trans: I wondered how we could afford such a fine lifestyle without a father in the house.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

meanings.en: to teach; to tell; to show
meanings.note: Ichidan verb.
Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Standard word for family.

examples.text: 週末は家族と過ごします。
examples.trans: I spend weekends with my family.
Everyone in my family is doing well.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Core everyday reassurance or check covering safety, health, and reliability.

examples.text: 心配しないで、大丈夫だよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is fine.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。

meanings.note: Na-adjective; the thing liked is marked with が or は.

examples.text: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

meanings.note: Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
